title: The reduced geometric fibre locus commutes with base change
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ and $g:T\prime\to T$ be arbitrary morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Put $X\prime=X\times_TT\prime$ and let $f\prime:X\prime\to T\prime$ be the base change of $f$ [def-pc-base-change]. For $t\in T$ and $t\prime\in T\prime$, use geometric fibres over chosen algebraic closures of the respective residue fields [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Then, as subsets of $T\prime$, $$\{t\prime\in T\prime\mid X\prime_{\bar t\prime}\text{ is reduced}\}=g^{-1}\bigl(\{t\in T\mid X_{\bar t}\text{ is reduced}\}\bigr).$$ Here reduced means that every local ring has no nonzero nilpotents [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Empty fibres are included; no flatness, finite-presentation or surjectivity assumption on either morphism is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0576 (lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced); its proof applies varieties.tex Tag 0384 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-upstairs) to the residue-field extension. Formulation via reduced geometric fibres uses varieties.tex Tag 035X (lemma-geometrically-reduced), (2) iff (6), in positive characteristic and Tag 020I (lemma-perfect-reduced) in characteristic zero.

proof.text: Fix $t'\in T'$, put $t=g(t')$, $k=\kappa(t)$ and $L=\kappa(t')$; the embedding $k\to L$ is supplied by [def-weil-residue-field]. Choose algebraic closures $E/k$ and $F/L$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Choose an affine open cover $X_t=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-fibre-affine-chart-test] first with $g=\mathrm{id}_T$, point $t$ and $H=E$ (so its two residue fields are both $k$), then with the actual $g$, point $t'$ and $H=F$. For the identity base change, the first projection $X\times_TT\to X$ and the map $(1_X,f):X\to X\times_TT$ are inverse by the uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product]; hence its $E$-fibre is precisely $X_{\bar t}$ up to the canonical isomorphism. Use the same affine cover of $X_t$ in both applications, and give $F$ its composite $k\to L\to F$ structure. It identifies the two reducedness conditions with, respectively, reducedness of every $A_i\otimes_kE$ and of every $A_i\otimes_kF$. In particular, it supplies the required fibre identifications and the covering assertion, without assuming either morphism flat.

source.place: Tag 0576, first sentence of proof, with the affine chart test

proof.text: Both $E$ and $F$ are perfect. In characteristic $p>0$, for every $a$ the polynomial $Z^p-a$ has a root by algebraic closedness [def-weil-algebraic-closure], so Frobenius is surjective. Characteristic zero is the other case of perfectness. Regard $F$ as a $k$-field via $k\to L\to F$.

source.place: Tag 00I4, perfect-field hypothesis verified from the definition

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-trf-perfect-scalars-reducedness-comparison] to the $k$-algebra $A_i$ and the perfect extensions $E/k$ and $F/k$. It gives $A_i\otimes_kE$ reduced if and only if $A_i\otimes_kF$ reduced. Taking the conjunction over the same affine cover and using step 1 proves $X_{\bar t}$ reduced if and only if $X'_{\bar t'}$ reduced, in both directions.

source.place: Tag 00I4, scalar comparison via a common overfield

proof.text: Membership in the inverse image on the right of the statement is exactly reducedness of $X_{\overline{g(t')}}$. The pointwise equivalence therefore proves the equality by extensionality. The closures in step 1 were arbitrary. For an empty fibre the affine cover may be empty, and both conjunctions and all local-ring conditions are vacuous. No flatness, finite-presentation or surjectivity hypothesis was introduced.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0576 and varieties.tex Tag 0384; direct affine proof with a common extension of the two algebraic closures, using algebra.tex Tags 00I4 and 05CK.
